name: Saints Cornelius and Cyprian
history: A pope and a bishop of Carthage, allies in a time of persecution, both named in the Roman Canon. When Christians who had denied the faith under threat of death sought to return, Cornelius and Cyprian upheld both mercy and penance against a rigorist schism. Cornelius died in exile in 253; Cyprian was beheaded in 258.
life: Under the Emperor Decius in 250 many Christians gave way and offered sacrifice to the gods. When the persecution eased, the Church had to decide how to receive them back. Cornelius, elected Bishop of Rome in 251, held that the lapsed could be reconciled after penance. The priest Novatian, taking a harsher view, had himself made a rival bishop. Cyprian, a rhetorician who had become a Christian as a grown man and soon afterwards bishop of Carthage, stood by Cornelius and wrote his treatise On the Unity of the Catholic Church. Cornelius was exiled to Centumcellae, on the coast north of Rome, where he died in 253. Under the Emperor Valerian, Cyprian was arrested and condemned. Hearing the sentence, he answered thanks be to God, and had twenty-five gold pieces given to his executioner.
prayerTo: Saints Cornelius and Cyprian, shepherds in a time of trial, you held together mercy for the fallen and fidelity to Christ. Pray for the unity of the Church, for those who have drifted from the faith and long to return, and for me, that I may never be ashamed of Christ, whatever it may cost. Amen.
penance: Go to confession, or make a careful examination of conscience tonight, and pray for someone who has fallen away from the faith.
meditation: Cyprian wrote that no one can have God for his Father who does not have the Church for his mother. How do you love the Church, with all her weakness?
prayer: May the feast of the blessed Martyrs and Bishops Cornelius and Cyprian, protect us, O Lord, we beseech You, and may their holy prayer recommend us unto You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
